tour.name: Bali Sea Temples Private Tour: Tanah Lot, Uluwatu, Kecak Fire Dance & Jimbaran Seafood Dinner
tour.subtitle: A private afternoon and evening on Bali's coast with a licensed guide and car: Tanah Lot temple on its rock in the sea, the clifftop temple of Uluwatu above the Indian Ocean, the Kecak fire dance at sunset, and a seafood dinner with your feet in the sand at Jimbaran Bay.

tour.overview:
In the 16th century the Hindu priest Dang Hyang Nirartha travelled along Bali's coast founding sea temples, each in sight of the next, to protect the island from the spirits of the sea. Two of them are among the most spectacular sights in Bali: Tanah Lot, on a rock surrounded by the sea at high tide, and Uluwatu, on the edge of a cliff at the island's southern tip. Every evening at Uluwatu, as the sun sets, dancers perform the Kecak, a hypnotic chant-and-fire version of the Ramayana created in the 1930s.

This private tour combines both temples, the Kecak dance and a beach dinner, with a licensed Balinese guide and a car.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 8 hours (afternoon and evening)
• Start and end: your hotel in south Bali
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy; some steps at Uluwatu

WHAT YOU SEE
• Tanah Lot temple.
• Uluwatu temple and its cliffs.
• The Kecak fire dance.
• Jimbaran Bay at night.

WHY THIS WORKS
We visit Tanah Lot at low tide in the early afternoon, when you can reach the rock, and reach Uluwatu in time for the sunset dance, with reserved seats.

WHO IT SUITS
Couples, families and anyone staying in south Bali.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you want the rice fields and culture of the interior, choose our Ubud tour.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Non-Hindus cannot enter the inner temples at Tanah Lot or Uluwatu; you see them from outside. The monkeys of Uluwatu are notorious for snatching glasses, phones and hats. Traffic between Tanah Lot and Uluwatu can take 1 hour 30 minutes.

days.name: Tanah Lot, Uluwatu temple, the Kecak fire dance at sunset and a seafood dinner in Jimbaran
days.description:
What to expect: Bali's two most famous sea temples, a sunset dance and a beach dinner, with a licensed guide, private car, tickets and dinner.

Your guide and driver collect you at your hotel at about 13:00 and drive to Tanah Lot on the west coast. The temple stands on a rock just off the shore, surrounded by the sea at high tide and reachable on foot at low tide. At its base, a freshwater spring flows from the rock, and priests bless visitors with its holy water and a grain of rice on the forehead. In the cave opposite live black-and-white sea snakes, believed to guard the temple. Your guide tells you the story of the priest Nirartha, who is said to have turned his sash into the snakes.

You drive south, through Kuta and across the Bukit peninsula, to Uluwatu, where the temple of Pura Luhur Uluwatu, one of Bali's six great directional temples, stands at the very edge of a limestone cliff 70 metres above the surf. You walk along the clifftop paths, past the temple gates, for views of the Indian Ocean and the waves breaking below.

As the sun sets, you take your seats in the open-air amphitheatre on the cliff for the Kecak dance. Seventy men in checked sarongs sit in circles and chant 'cak-cak-cak' in shifting rhythms, with no instruments, while dancers in gold and masks act out the story of Rama, Sita and the monkey general Hanuman, who ends the performance amid a circle of burning coconut husks. After the show, you drive down to Jimbaran Bay for a seafood dinner at a table on the sand – grilled fish, prawns, squid and clams with sambal and rice – by candlelight, with the planes landing over the bay. You are back at your hotel at about 21:00.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
13:00 – Pick-up at your hotel.
14:00 – Tanah Lot temple.
15:45 – Drive to Uluwatu.
17:00 – Uluwatu temple and clifftop walk.
18:00 – Kecak fire dance at sunset.
19:15 – Seafood dinner in Jimbaran.
21:00 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Times change slightly through the year with the sunset; we confirm them with you.
• At Uluwatu, store glasses and phones securely: the monkeys steal them to trade for food.
• Tanah Lot is best at low tide; we check the tide tables.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, temple entrances and sarongs, Kecak tickets, dinner, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: drinks with dinner, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: dinner.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Can we go inside the temples?
faq.answer: The inner sanctuaries are reserved for Hindu worshippers. You visit the outer courtyards, the clifftop paths and, at Tanah Lot at low tide, the spring at the foot of the rock.

faq.question: Are the tickets and dinner included?
faq.answer: Yes: both temple entrances with sarongs, the Kecak dance and dinner in Jimbaran.

faq.question: Is dinner included?
faq.answer: Yes, grilled seafood on the beach. Chicken and vegetarian dishes are available.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the fire dance, the sea snakes and the beach dinner. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. Tanah Lot has paved paths but the rock is reached over wet stones; Uluwatu has steps along the cliff.

faq.question: Are the monkeys a problem?
faq.answer: At Uluwatu they are bold thieves. Remove glasses and earrings and keep phones in a zipped bag; your guide helps.

faq.question: Will traffic be bad?
faq.answer: South Bali traffic is slow in the late afternoon; we plan generous time so you don't miss the sunset dance.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tips are appreciated in Bali but never required.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Light clothes covering shoulders and knees for the temples (sarongs are provided), and comfortable shoes.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: April to October for clear sunsets. In the rainy season, sunsets can be dramatic or cloudy.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
